mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is a chain isomer of butane (C4H10)?
mcqs.explanation: Chain isomerism involves compounds that have the same molecular formula but different carbon skeletons. n‑Butane and 2‑Methylpropane both have formula C4H10 but differ in the arrangement of the carbon chain, making them chain isomers. But‑1‑ene differs by a double bond (unsaturation) and 2‑Butanol differs by a functional group (alcohol), so they are not chain isomers of butane.

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds illustrates position isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: Position isomerism occurs when the functional group (or a substituent) occupies different positions on the same carbon skeleton. In 1‑butanol the –OH group is on carbon‑1, whereas in 2‑butanol it is on carbon‑2; the carbon chain remains unchanged. The other options represent chain isomerism (A), geometric isomerism (C), or different degrees of unsaturation (D).

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds are functional isomers of each other?
mcqs.explanation: Functional isomerism refers to compounds that have the same molecular formula but belong to different functional groups. Ethanol (an alcohol) and dimethyl ether (an ether) both have the formula C2H6O but differ in functional group, making them functional isomers. Options B and C are examples of structural (chain) isomerism, while D has different molecular formulas.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand stereoisomerism at the required level
mcqs.question: Consider the compound C2H2Cl2. Which of the following statements is true regarding its stereoisomerism?

options.A: It has no stereoisomers because both chlorines are attached to the same carbon atom.
options.B: It exists as a pair of enantiomers.
options.C: It exists as a pair of geometric (cis‑trans) isomers.
options.D: It has only one structural isomer.

mcqs.answer: It exists as a pair of geometric (cis‑trans) isomers.
mcqs.explanation: C2H2Cl2 can be 1,2‑dichloroethene. When the two chlorine atoms are attached to different carbon atoms, the molecule can have a cis arrangement (both Cl on the same side) or a trans arrangement (Cl on opposite sides). Hence it exhibits geometric (cis‑trans) stereoisomerism. Option A is wrong because the chlorines are on different carbons; B is wrong because there is no chiral centre; D is irrelevant to stereoisomerism.

mcqs.question: Isomerism is best defined as:

options.A: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different functional groups.
options.B: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different connectivity or spatial arrangement of atoms.
options.C: Compounds with the same empirical formula but different molecular weight.
options.D: Compounds that differ only in the number of carbon atoms.

mcqs.answer: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different connectivity or spatial arrangement of atoms.
mcqs.explanation: Isomerism encompasses all cases where compounds share the same molecular formula yet differ either in the way atoms are connected (structural isomerism) or in their three‑dimensional arrangement (stereoisomerism). Options A, C, and D describe other relationships that are not the definition of isomerism.

mcqs.question: Structural isomerism refers to:

options.A: Isomers differing only in the spatial arrangement around a double bond.
options.B: Isomers with different connectivity of atoms.
options.D: Molecules with the same connectivity but different rotation about single bonds.

mcqs.answer: Isomers with different connectivity of atoms.
mcqs.explanation: Structural (or constitutional) isomerism involves changes in the order in which atoms are bonded, leading to different skeletons or functional groups while keeping the molecular formula constant. Option A describes geometric (cis‑trans) isomerism, C describes optical isomerism, and D describes conformational isomerism, none of which are structural isomerism.

mcqs.question: Chain isomerism is a type of structural isomerism where the carbon skeleton differs. Which statement correctly distinguishes chain isomerism from functional isomerism?

options.A: Chain isomers have different functional groups, while functional isomers have the same carbon skeleton.
options.B: Chain isomers differ in the arrangement of the carbon chain, whereas functional isomers have different functional groups despite having the same molecular formula.
options.C: Both involve different positions of substituents on the same carbon chain.
options.D: Chain isomerism occurs only in aromatic compounds.

mcqs.answer: Chain isomers differ in the arrangement of the carbon chain, whereas functional isomers have different functional groups despite having the same molecular formula.
mcqs.explanation: In chain isomerism the carbon backbone is rearranged (e.g., n‑butane vs. isobutane). Functional isomerism keeps the carbon skeleton unchanged but changes the functional group (e.g., ethanol vs. dimethyl ether). Options A, C, and D are inaccurate descriptions of the two types of isomerism.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a position isomer of 1‑chloropropane (CH3CH2CH2Cl)?
mcqs.explanation: Position isomerism involves the same carbon skeleton with the functional group (or substituent) attached at a different carbon. 1‑chloropropane has the chlorine on carbon‑1; moving it to carbon‑2 gives 2‑chloropropane, which is the position isomer. 1‑bromopropane changes the halogen (different substituent), propane lacks a halogen, and 1‑chlorobutane has a different carbon skeleton.
